answer.rationale: Rollback is unavailable (mandatory security patch), so memory_b1's rollback playbook is off the table despite the release-timing correlation. The latency is on the write path during peak settlement traffic, so route_read_replicas (memory_b5) does not address the bottleneck. Regional failover (memory_b2) won't help if the cause is the new build or load, and it risks write disruption at peak. Circuit breaker (memory_b4) only applies if a downstream dependency is implicated, and fail-fast behavior could jeopardize the 'no lost writes' objective — I want its source record verified before considering it later. Memory_b3 (provisioning headroom before a peak) is the closest fit to sustained write-path pressure: adding capacity is reversible, preserves all writes, and buys time to diagnose whether the release caused a resource regression. Starting as a small guarded capacity increase with close monitoring of p99 and error rates rather than a broad rollout, since root cause is unconfirmed.
